definition: Reserved power of appointment is when the owner of the appointive assets gives the appointive assets away, but reserves to themselves a power of appointment (the ability to choose the beneficiaries of the property). In other words, it is when a donor gives property to a donee but keeps the power to decide who gets it in the future. For example, a grandmother gives her house to her grandchild but reserves the ability to decide what happens to the house once the grandchild is financially stable.
